Ivy: FYI new reranker int8 bring-up shows odd metrics: NDCG stable but MRR@10 down ~6%. run id run/2026-08-15/04
Ben: numbers?
Ivy: float MRR@10=0.439 -> int8 MRR@10=0.412, NDCG@10 unchanged.
Sofia: did we change holdout sampling or dedupe? small reordering can hit MRR a lot.
Ivy: spotted a bug in the eval harness: duplicate document ids in the holdout after a recent merge, duplicates get collapsed in float run path but dedup step skipped for int8 path due to race in parallel sampling. Example: same doc repeated at different ranks causing artificial tie-break sensitivity.
Ben: that explains top1 flips. Any quick repro?
Ivy: yes pushed a minimal repro and bench diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/912. Local 2k probe running now.
eval-bot: shadowbench started sb-912 est 1h logs -> /ops/bench/sb-912
Sofia: while that's running also try PTQ per_channel true and calib=8192 to see if quant noise compounds.
Ben: local probe results: fixing dedupe restores MRR from .412 -> .436; per_channel + calib boosts to .442 (slightly above float).
Ivy: plan: 1) patch eval harness to ensure deterministic dedupe before split, 2) add regression unit that injects duplicate doc ids, 3) adopt per_channel PTQ as default for rerankers, 4) rerun full bench.
Sofia: add a note: eval harness must treat float and quant paths identically (no conditional fast-paths that change data ordering).
Ivy: opened PR #912 with harness fix + unit + bench regen.
eval-bot: sb-912 finished: patched vs baseline NDCG@10 +0.1%, MRR@10 +5.8% (patched wins)
Ben: great catch, thanks. Merge after perf sign-off.
